Editorial standards

How we research and review products

Every recommendation on ProSiteGuide is measured against what a small law firm actually needs and checked against the vendor's current, official information. Here is our process, in full.

See our guidesAffiliate disclosure

Our commitments

  • Primary sources onlyOfficial pricing pages, documentation and help centers.
  • No invented resultsNo made-up tests, scores, statistics or testimonials.
  • Independent verdictsCommissions never affect rankings.
  • Dated informationPrices labelled with the month they were checked.
Our criteria

What we evaluate, and why it matters to a firm

We start from a firm's requirements, not a vendor's feature list.

Security

SSL, malware protection, firewalls, two-factor login and how client inquiries are protected.

Backups and recovery

How often backups run, where they are stored and how quickly a site can be restored.

Performance and reliability

Infrastructure, caching and CDN options that keep a site fast and online.

Support

The channels and hours actually offered, and whether support covers common firm problems.

True cost

Renewal prices, required add-ons and contract terms, not just the introductory offer.

Ownership and portability

Whether you control your domain, data and site, and can move them if you leave.

Our process

From question to published guide

Define the decision

We identify the question a firm is trying to answer and the criteria that matter.

Gather primary sources

We read official pricing, documentation, terms and relevant bar or government guidance.

Compare like for like

Plans are compared at the tier a small firm would realistically buy, including renewals.

Write and fact-check

Claims are checked against sources, and sources are linked in the article.

Update over time

We revisit guides when prices, plans or features change, and update the date.

Sources we rely on

Where our facts come from

We link sources directly in each article so you can verify them. Typical sources include:

  • Vendor pricing pages, documentation, knowledge bases and terms of service
  • Bar associations and professional-responsibility resources, such as ABA formal opinions
  • Government and standards bodies, such as the FTC, CISA, ADA.gov and the W3C
  • Search engine documentation, such as Google Search Central
  • Registry and registrar policies for domain extensions

What we don't do

  • No fabricated testingWe describe hands-on results only when we actually have them.
  • No made-up scores or statisticsIf we can't source a number, it doesn't appear.
  • No rewritten press releasesVendor marketing claims are checked against documentation.
  • No paid placementsVendors can't buy a position in our guides.
Experience and research

We say which is which

Some guidance comes from building and maintaining law firm websites. Most comparisons are research-based. We aim to make the difference clear, and we never present research as personal testing.

When a guide touches legal ethics or compliance, such as confidentiality of client inquiries, it stays general, cites official sources and recommends checking your state bar's rules.

Updates and corrections

Information changes, and so do our guides

Each article shows its last-updated date, and prices are labelled with the month they were checked. If you find an error, please tell us. Every report is reviewed and the article is corrected where needed.

Questions

About our reviews

Do affiliate commissions affect your rankings?

No. We include products we don't earn from when they are the better fit. See our affiliate disclosure.

Do you test every product yourselves?

No, and we don't claim to. Most comparisons are based on official documentation, pricing and terms. Where we draw on hands-on experience, we say so.

Why don't you give star ratings or scores?

Scores imply measured testing. Without consistent, repeatable tests behind them, we think clear trade-offs and "best for" guidance are more honest and more useful.

How often are guides updated?

Whenever we learn that prices, plans or features have changed, and during regular reviews of our most-read guides.

Spotted something out of date?

Help us keep every guide accurate.

Send a correction
